assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation reframes drug discovery: small molecules recruit E3 ligases to induce ubiquitination and proteasomal destruction of targets, including ones without conventional binding pockets. The idea is original, chemically clear, and has produced a clinical pipeline.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the PROTAC concept (with Sakamoto); Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target underpins molecular glue degraders. Ciulli, Gray and others made key later advances, but a three-person limit forces a choice between concept and mechanism origins.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of independent validation, many degraders in clinical trials and mechanistic understanding of ternary-complex formation. Clinical approval of a degrader would strengthen but is not essential to recognition; timing looks ripe.
uncertainties: Whether a prize should split PROTAC concept from molecular-glue mechanism (cereblon) is unresolved.
Ciulli and Gray are strong contributors who would be excluded by the three-laureate limit.
Clinical outcome evidence is still maturing; I have not independently verified current trial status.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics made ab initio dynamics feasible, so bond breaking, solvation and condensed-phase reactivity could be simulated from electronic structure. Its influence on theoretical chemistry, materials and liquids is foundational and lasting, as the methods underlying much of modern simulation.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper is clearly credited to Car and Parrinello; a clean two-person configuration with no real attribution dispute.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of use and independent extension. Computational chemistry has been recognised recently (2013, and 2024 for protein structure), which may reduce urgency but not the merit.
uncertainties: Parrinello also appears on metadynamics and machine-learned potentials entries, so the committee may see his contributions as better recognised in a different combination.
Prior recent computational prizes may weigh against timing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editing chemically converts one DNA base to another without double-strand cleavage, using deaminase chemistry coupled to programmable targeting. It is a clear chemical-biology invention that complements the 2020 CRISPR prize and has therapeutic reach.
assessment.attribution: David Liu led the conceptual and practical development; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead trainees on the cytosine and adenine editors. A sole laureate is defensible given the inventive leadership, though Komor/Gaudelli credit could be raised.
assessment.maturity: Base editors have been replicated widely and entered clinical trials, with early patient data. Interpretation of the discovery is stable; recognition seems timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would prefer prime editing (B038) or a combined Liu prize instead is unclear to me.
Overlap with the 2020 genome-editing prize could be viewed as incremental by some members.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of cells brought physical-chemistry concepts (multivalency, phase behavior) to cell biology, and has changed how intracellular compartmentalization is thought about. Very broad influence.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman's 2009 P granule work is the clear origin; Rosen's multivalent-interaction phase-separation work provided the physical-chemical framework. Pappu and Mittag are strong contributors but the cap of three limits the set.
assessment.maturity: The field is large and productive, but debate remains on physiological relevance versus in vitro droplets, and on what material states are present in vivo. Possibly somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Disputes over the physiological significance of condensates and of artefacts from overexpression.
Credit allocation between Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen and the theorists is not settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers rapidly reached silicon-competitive efficiencies in solution-processed cells, an unusually rapid and consequential materials discovery with large energy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cells; Park's solid-state cell and Snaith's mesostructured and planar devices drove efficiency. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis are also plausible, so attribution is contested.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency gains are independently confirmed worldwide, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercialization remain open, so timing may be premature.
uncertainties: Attribution is contentious among six credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Massively parallel sequencing-by-synthesis transformed biology and medicine by reducing sequencing cost by orders of magnitude; the underlying chemistry of reversible terminators and clonal clusters is a real chemical invention.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman originated the Solexa chemistry and single-molecule approach; Rothberg's 454 pyrosequencing and others contributed to the field's parallel-platform development. A two-person prize is defensible but competing platforms muddy it.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with decades of independent validation and unmatched impact. Sanger sequencing was already recognised in 1980.
uncertainties: Several competing technologies (454, Illumina, nanopore) make the single most decisive credit unclear.
Some members may regard it as more biology/technology than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion lets cells incorporate noncanonical amino acids site-specifically through orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs, a clear and original chemical-biology invention widely used in protein engineering and biophysics.
assessment.attribution: Schultz pioneered the first orthogonal pairs in vivo (with Lei Wang); Chin extended it to multicellular organisms and to quadruplet codons and ribosome engineering. Wang and Yokoyama also have strong claims.
assessment.maturity: Methods are widely replicated for two decades; applications are expanding, so recognition is timely though no single transformative application dominates.
uncertainties: Who the decisive contributors are among Schultz, Wang, Chin, Mehl and Yokoyama is not clear.
Impact is more as a toolkit than a conceptual shift.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reversible m6A RNA methylation and its writers, erasers and readers opened the field of epitranscriptomics, linking RNA chemistry to gene regulation and showing that RNA modification is dynamic.
assessment.attribution: He identified FTO as an m6A demethylase and developed key chemical-biology approaches; Jaffrey and Rechavi developed transcriptome-wide mapping (m6A-seq/miCLIP). Jia, Meyer, Dominissini, Yang are also credited, so the three-name cap leaves unresolved allocation.
assessment.maturity: Field is large with mechanistic confirmation, but some mapping methods and the FTO substrate biology remain debated; maturity moderate.
uncertainties: Debate over FTO substrate specificity and the reliability of antibody-based mapping.
The crowded credit set means a fair three-person configuration is unclear.
